case_name: Sanju Midha vs Prachi on 23 September, 2010
facts_of_case: Husband-petitioner challenging the order allowing wife-respondent's application for maintenance pendente lite and composite litigation expenses. Husband has no permanent source of income, maintains himself by selling cow milk. Wife is well-educated and earns more than Rs.25,000/- per month.

legal_principles.principle: A spouse's income is relevant in determining maintenance
legal_principles.held: It has further been contended that in the peculiar circumstances of the case, husband is entitled for maintenance from the wife since wife's income is more than the husband's income and wife is not entitled for any maintenance.

legal_principles.principle: A spouse's ability to maintain themselves is relevant in determining maintenance
legal_principles.held: Learned counsel for the husband further stated that husband is having only one cow and by selling the milk of one cow, the husband is anyhow maintaining himself.

outcome.final_order: Husband-petitioner directed to pay Rs. 7,000/- per month as maintenance pendente lite and Rs. 10,000/- towards composite litigation expenses.
